hero.eyebrow: Off the route · to be used to
hero.h1: The thing that stopped being strange
hero.lede: One letter from the other cloud and nothing like it. This is not a past habit — it is a present state, a description of how you are right now. It takes a noun or an -ing form, never an infinitive, and it runs straight through NOW instead of stopping short of it.

sections.label: Cloud briefing
sections.title: When to use it
sections.lead: One letter from its neighbour and nothing like it. This is not a past habit — it is a present state, a description of how you are right now, and it takes a noun or an -ing form, never an infinitive.

cards.head: Something has stopped being strange
cards.body: The state of finding a thing normal, having once found it odd.

cards.head: It takes a noun or an -ing
cards.body: Never an infinitive. This is the error that gives it away.

cards.head: It moves through the tenses
cards.body: It is an ordinary adjective phrase, so be does the usual work.
cards.ex: "I was used to it by then." · "You'll be used to it soon."

cards.head: Get used to = the process
cards.body: Becoming familiar, rather than already being familiar.

cards.head: The negative is common and useful
cards.body: Most often you are explaining why something is hard.

cards.head: It says nothing about the past
cards.body: Unlike its neighbour, it makes no claim that anything has stopped.
cards.ex: "I'm used to living alone." — and I still do

cards.head: Affirmative
cards.body: subject + am / is / are + used to + noun or -ing

cards.head: Negative
cards.body: subject + am / is / are + not + used to + …

cards.head: Questions
cards.body: Am / Is / Are + subject + used to + …?

charts.head: The three forms, side by side
charts.note: This is the chart worth learning by heart. Three phrases, one letter apart, three different jobs.

head: Form
Means
Example
rows: a past habit that has stopped
"I used to live here." — I don't now
a present state: it is normal to me
"I'm used to living here." — I still do

charts.head: What can follow it
charts.note: After used to in this phrase comes a thing, never an action in its plain form. If you can put it there, you can put an -ing there.

head: Follows with
Example
Right?
rows: No — this is the classic error

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this phrase is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: I'm used to get up early.
I'm used to getting up early.
After this to comes a thing, not an action. The -ing makes it a thing.
The phrase needs be. Without it you have accidentally written the other form.
I used to live here. / I'm used to living here.
Both are English and they mean opposite things. Decide which you mean.

sections.label: The fork in the path
sections.title: Which of the two do you want?

charts.note: They differ by one word and they point in opposite directions. Used to looks back and says something ended. Be used to looks at now and says something is normal.

head: Question
be used to + -ing
used to + infinitive
rows:
It was true, and stopped.
"I used to hate the cold."
Yes: was used to, will be used to.

charts.example: The pair that decides it: "I used to live alone" — I have a flatmate now. "I'm used to living alone" — I still do, and it suits me. One word apart, and the second one is the only one that tells you where I live today.

sections.label: Trail markers
sections.title: Signal words

signals.head: The giveaway that you want the other one

sections.example: A useful habit: try replacing the phrase with familiar with. If the sentence still works, you want be used to. If it collapses, you want used to.

sections.label: Interactive
sections.title: A state that runs through now

diagram.intro: The brown peg is where it started — the first day, when the thing was still strange. From there the band runs on, and the dots grow more solid as it becomes ordinary. Crucially it does not stop at NOW: it goes straight through and out the other side, because this is a description of how you are, not a report of something finished. The violet zone above is that present state. Click either to see it in a sentence.

quiz.explain: After be used to comes a noun or an -ing form. Getting is the -ing.

quiz.prompt: She _____ the cold — she grew up in Oslo.
quiz.explain: Be + used to describes how she is now. Used to would say she doesn't any more.

quiz.prompt: I _____ live in Rome, but I moved back in 2019.
quiz.explain: A past habit that has stopped, with no be: used to live.

quiz.prompt: I _____ living alone — it suits me.
quiz.explain: Be used to + -ing: a present state. It says nothing has stopped.

quiz.prompt: It was strange at first, but I _____ it. (get)
quiz.explain: Get used to is the becoming; be used to is the being.
Yet points at now, so the present of be: aren't used to.
Are + subject + used to. Did you use to would ask about a stopped habit.

quiz.prompt: By the end of the winter I _____ the dark mornings.
quiz.hint: A past state, not a habit.
quiz.explain: Be used to takes the past of be when the state itself is in the past.

quiz.prompt: You _____ it in a week or two.
quiz.explain: Get used to carries the becoming, and will puts it in the future.

quiz.prompt: I'm used to _____ nights, so the shift doesn't bother me.
quiz.explain: An -ing form turns the action into a thing, which is what this to needs.

quiz.prompt: He _____ a beard, but he shaved it off.
quiz.explain: A past state that has changed, with no be: used to have.

quiz.prompt: She's not used to _____ so much.
quiz.explain: The negative changes nothing about what follows: still a noun or an -ing.

quiz.prompt: I _____ the traffic here. It still shocks me.
quiz.explain: Still shocks me puts it firmly in the present, so the present of be.

quiz.prompt: We _____ swim in the lake every summer.
quiz.explain: No be, and an infinitive follows: a stopped past habit.

results: Clean run. You never put an infinitive after this one, and you can hear which cloud a sentence wants.
Solid progress. Worth a look at the other cloud before you go on.
Good first attempt. The three-forms chart is the part to read again.
